terms.gloss: in exchange for, in return for
evidence: Ter. Ph. 336: prō maleficiō … beneficium … reddere
Tac. Ann. 4.18: prō grātiā odium redditur
terms.comment: What is given or paid back for something: prō meritō, as one deserves.

terms.grammar: construction: the price in the ablative, with verbs of buying, selling and costing
evidence: Ter. Ad. 191: minīs vīgintī tū illam ēmistī
terms.comment: “For how much?” is the genitive of value, quantī?. With mūtāre the thing exchanged stands in the ablative (see trade).

evidence: Catull. 13.9: sed contrā accipiēs merōs amōrēs

phrases.latin: Alere nōlunt hominem edācem; et sapiunt, meā quidem sententiā, prō maleficiō sī beneficium summum nōlunt reddere.
phrases.english: They don’t want to feed a greedy man; and they are wise, in my opinion, if they don’t want to return the greatest kindness for a wrong.

phrases.latin: Nōn potest satis prō meritō ab illō tibi referrī grātia.
phrases.english: He can never thank you enough for what you have done.

phrases.latin: Minīs vīgintī tū illam ēmistī; quae rēs tibi vertat male. Argentī tantum dabitur.
phrases.english: You bought her for twenty minae (and may it bring you bad luck): that much money will be paid.
Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?

phrases.latin: nam beneficia eō ūsque laeta sunt dum videntur exolvī posse: ubi multum antevēnēre prō grātiā odium redditur
phrases.english: favours are welcome only as long as it seems they can be repaid; once they far outrun that, hatred is returned for gratitude
but in return you will get pure love

sources: Lewis & Short: pro · Lewis & Short: contra
